clue.text: Sort of golf shot, possibly a drive

definitions.meaning: in golf, the stroke played onto the green from the fairway
the road or driveway leading up to a house is its way in

explanation.surface: A golfer wondering whether a tee shot counts as one kind of stroke or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' looks like more golf, but the second sense is the private road up to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a way of getting near: a stroke to the green, and the road leading to a building.

clue.text: Bent cop able to provide harmless drug

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman able to supply a drug that does no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as British slang for corrupt, describing the cop, but it tells you to rearrange COP ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no active ingredient, given for its psychological effect, is a harmless drug.

clue.text: Sent our part out to us

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dispatched their share of something to a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' looks like a past tense verb but is old slang for thrilled; 'out' rearranges the letters, and 'to' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sent is old slang for being in ecstasy, carried away with delight.

clue.text: A mount? Arranged to get on top of that

parts.note: taken as written
a swell is a rise in the ground, a gentle mount or hill

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a horse is set up so they can climb aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A SWELL is a mount; 'Arranged' tells you to move the space between the words, so the same letters read as a two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means also or in addition, the same as saying on top of that.

clue.text: Produce this plant from "Simple Kit"

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb
Kit is a pet form of the first name Christopher

explanation.surface: A gardener told to grow something from a basic seed packet.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Simple Kit' looks like a product name, but it is two words to be translated: a simple is a herb, and Kit is short for Christopher.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for baneberry, a woodland plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Cripes! That's bad condensation

indicators.note: bad here means spoiled or wrong, so the letters of the exclamation are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming in dismay at damp on the windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condensation' suggests moisture on glass, but here it means a shortened version of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary is a condensing of a longer text into its essentials.

clue.text: Cooking pots containing most of the finest sweetbread

indicators.note: containing means the pots hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: pans are pots used for cooking

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the cream is the finest part of anything, as in the cream of society

explanation.surface: A recipe in which pans hold the best cut of offal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetbread' sounds like a pastry, but it is the culinary name for a gland; 'the finest' is the cream of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbread is the culinary name for the pancreas or thymus gland of a young animal.

clue.text: Revolutionary college near a trendy part of London

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
LSE is the London School of Economics
taken as written

explanation.surface: A radical university sitting near a fashionable district.
explanation.walkthrough: CHELSEA is a fashionable district of west London, famed for the King's Road in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: This west London district has long been known as fashionable and stylish.

clue.text: Baseball player taking a breather

definitions.meaning: the fielder placed between second and third base
a brief pause or halt, read as two words

explanation.surface: A baseball player pausing for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into two words: a short stop is a quick pause.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielding position between second and third base, and also a brief halt for rest.

clue.text: Repeatedly get one's hands on fruit

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece is said twice in a row

parts.note: to paw is to handle something clumsily with the hands

explanation.surface: Someone keeps grabbing at the fruit bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya, a tropical fruit, is also known by this doubled name.

clue.text: Mexican worker needing protection of tough chaps, perhaps

definitions.text: Mexican worker needing protection of tough chaps, perhaps

parts.words: Mexican worker needing protection of tough chaps, perhaps
parts.note: chaps reads as tough men, but means the leather leggings a cattle hand wears to protect his legs

explanation.walkthrough: 'chaps' suggests men, but chaps are leather over-trousers worn by cowhands on Mexican and American ranches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle hand on a Mexican ranch, who wears protective leather leggings in the saddle.

clue.text: Where King or Queen gets rejected by the people

definitions.text: Where King or Queen gets rejected by the people

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the royal letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER stands for Edwardus Rex or Elizabeth Regina, a king or a queen
the public is the people as a whole

explanation.surface: A state where the monarchy is voted out by its citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it: 'gets rejected' reverses ER to RE, followed by PUBLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A state without a monarch, where power rests with the people, is one that has thrown off royalty.

clue.text: Game's quickly followed by cake and fruit

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game, with the possessive S
to cake is to harden or set solid

explanation.surface: Tea after a match: the game is soon followed by cake and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cake' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to set hard; 'quickly followed by' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A russet is a variety of apple with rough brownish skin.

clue.text: Backward type, retaining nothing

indicators.note: retaining means the reversed word holds the next piece inside it
backward means the word for type is read from right to left

parts.note: a norm is a standard type or pattern
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dim person who remembers nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, a slow-witted person with an empty head, and also the wordplay: 'Backward' turns NORM to MRON, which holds O.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulting word for a foolish person, once used for someone of slow mind.

clue.text: Moderate Russian chaps against being repressed by ruler

parts.note: men are chaps

indicators.note: being repressed means held down inside, so the ruler surrounds the letter for against

parts.note: a sheik is an Arab ruler
V is versus, against

explanation.surface: Moderate Russian men opposed to being kept down by their ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like a verb but describes the Russian faction; V is the usual crossword shorthand for versus, against.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mensheviks were the moderate wing of the Russian Social Democrats, opposed to the Bolsheviks.

clue.text: Vulgar characters in show

parts.note: broad humour is coarse or vulgar
the cast is the set of characters in a play

explanation.surface: Coarse figures appearing in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' reads as a noun at the end of the surface, but it is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a programme on radio or television is to put it on air for people to see.

clue.text: Athens, for example — or New York or Washington?

definitions.meaning: ancient Athens was an independent city ruling its own territory
each name is both a US city and a US state

explanation.surface: Athens is an example, but would New York or Washington count too?
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: New York and Washington each name both a city and a state.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign city with its own territory, like ancient Athens; the US names are cities and states at once.

clue.text: Neat tie — light and dark blue combination

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a bridge ties or links two things

explanation.surface: A smart necktie in two shades of blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge's colour is light blue and Oxford's dark blue; the answer joins the two universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge sports teams wear light blue and Oxford dark blue, and this word names the two universities together.

clue.text: Turn on partners and be lacking in discrimination?

indicators.note: turn means flip round, so the word on is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
North and South are partners in bridge
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: Someone told to arouse a partner and ends up showing no preference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses ON to NO; N and S are the North-South partnership at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating men and women alike means showing no prejudice on grounds of gender.

clue.text: Frank's an old fool

definitions.meaning: in old usage a born simpleton or idiot

explanation.surface: Frank is described as an elderly idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means unaffected and candid, and in old usage was a noun for a simpleton.

clue.text: What a hawk may do to duck

definitions.meaning: a falcon swoops down on its prey
to bend down quickly to avoid something

explanation.surface: A bird of prey dives on a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the hawk's prey but is the verb meaning bend down.
explanation.definitionFit: Falconers use the word for a hawk's dive on prey; it also means to bend the body forward and down.

clue.text: Not in a position to make a settlement

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a post is a position, a job or station

explanation.surface: Someone unable to afford to settle a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' suggests paying a bill, but it is a remote colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote frontier station or small colony far from the centre is an isolated settlement.

clue.text: Insight of the French primate set over Catholic University

indicators.note: in a down clue, set over means placed above the following pieces

parts.note: an ape is a primate
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A French thinker's insight about a monkey seated above a Catholic college.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a French word for a glimpse or insight, which is why the clue adds 'of the French'.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means a quick glimpse or perceptive summary.

clue.text: Popular song's meaningless words

parts.note: hot means in demand or popular
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A hit song's lyrics are nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty talk, words with no substance, is idiomatically something insubstantial like warm breath.

clue.text: Hostile place east of China?

indicators.note: east of in an across clue means placed to the right of

parts.note: china is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, and an oppo is a mate or colleague
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A location lying east of China that is unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country but is rhyming slang for a mate, giving OPPO, British slang for a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing someone in opposition, as an opponent does, means being against or hostile.

clue.text: Gallery or museum hard for monarch to enter

indicators.note: to enter means the monarch goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a monarch
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gallery or museum hard for the sovereign to get into.
explanation.walkthrough: ER enters V AND A H after the V, giving V-ER-ANDAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery can mean a roofed open platform along the side of a house, like a porch.

clue.text: Sense of occasion

definitions.meaning: a cause or ground for something

explanation.surface: A feeling for when something matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sanity or good judgement and also the cause or ground for an action.

clue.text: Judge it likely to hold this Highlander back

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in reverse order
to hold means the letters are held within the words that precede it

explanation.surface: A judge thinks it probable they can detain a Scottish man.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are hidden in 'judgE IT LIKely', read backwards. 'Highlander' means a Scottish soldier in a kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A man in a kilt, especially a soldier of a Highland regiment, is nicknamed after his dress.

clue.text: Way in which one may observe bar game

indicators.note: the way is the container, and the bar can be seen inside it

parts.note: a route is a way
a let is a hindrance or bar, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A path where one can see a pub game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it means an obstruction, the sense kept in the legal phrase without let or hindrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino game in which a ball settles in a numbered slot on a spinning wheel.
